clue.text: See 23
By coming between two lecturers, is Mark's missus giving trouble, or wee Jimmy?

definitions.text: missus giving trouble, or wee Jimmy?

indicators.note: coming between means sliding into the middle of the pair that follows

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lecturer, and a don is a university teacher
by in the sense of on, as in near or upon
M is the abbreviation for mark, the 's being link

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man's wife is causing difficulty between two academics, or whether a little Scot is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming between' places the first piece inside the pair. In Cockney rhyming slang 'trouble' (and strife) is the wife, and 'Jimmy' (Riddle) is a piddle, or wee.
explanation.definitionFit: Both rhyming-slang terms are examples of London speech, so the clue's question mark marks a definition by example.

clue.text: The local comic editor's left very happy to do the Locomotion?

indicators.note: left in the sense of gone away, so the editor's letters drop out

parts.note: chuffed is British slang for very pleased

explanation.surface: A local comedian is delighted that his editor has gone and dances the Locomotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The local comic' gives a second definition: in dialect a chuff is a clown or boor. The Locomotion is a 1960s dance, but here it means puffing like a steam engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam engine makes this puffing noise as it moves, so moving like a locomotive is a fair playful sense.

clue.text: Quite a wait to be able to welcome New Woman

indicators.note: welcome in the sense of taking a guest in, so the following letter goes inside

parts.note: a long wait is ages

explanation.surface: It takes a long while before a new woman can be greeted.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, so it stands for any woman in the clue.

clue.text: In restaurant, maybe yelling because of painful condition

parts.note: yelling makes a din
in as in suffering in some condition, caused by it
gout is a painful joint condition

explanation.surface: Someone yells in a restaurant because their gout is playing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal away from home, typically at a restaurant, so the clue gives an example with a question-like maybe.

clue.text: Now a Brahma worshipper is hidden, mysteriously in full view within

indicators.note: within puts the next piece inside the rearranged letters
mysteriously suggests the letters are disguised, so they are rearranged

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal, viewable by all

explanation.surface: A Brahma devotee is concealed, yet somehow in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mysteriously' rearranges IS HIDDEN, and 'within' sets U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Converted to the Hindu faith, whose trinity includes Brahma, so someone now worshipping him has been converted.

clue.text: One running through Devon in white ignored

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the following words

explanation.surface: Something running through Devon dressed in white goes unnoticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is something that runs, and this one flows through Devon to the sea at Teignmouth.

clue.text: It was difficult to call disciplines to order

indicators.note: to order means to arrange, so these letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A boss struggling to bring staff discipline into line.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing or judging verdict where the judges disagree, given when the result was close and hard to call.

clue.text: Registration for post dispatched in a panic?

indicators.note: letters in a panic are flustered and jumbled, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic last-minute posting of a registered letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' looks like mail, but it is a job, and registration is standing for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing as an applicant for a position or office, so it is registering to be considered for a job.

clue.text: See 13
Sin spun out with lubricant, (two?) non-traditional alternatives to newspaper

indicators.note: out in the sense of out of order or wrong, so the letters of the words around it are rearranged together

explanation.surface: Some sin is drawn out with the help of a lubricant, apparently in place of reading the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles SIN SPUN and LUBRICANT together. The '(two?)' allows for the plural: the riddle's new answer involves more than one nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuns' habits are black and white and an embarrassing setting turns them red all over, a modern spoof answer to the riddle.

clue.text: Still with chance of winning trophy, shown red card for foul

parts.words: Still with chance of winning trophy
parts.note: a team still in the competition is in
a footballer shown a red card is sent off

explanation.surface: A footballer whose side are still in the cup is sent off for a foul.
explanation.walkthrough: The foul is from snooker and billiards, not football: it is potting the cue ball off another ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In snooker, sending the white into a pocket off an object ball is a foul shot.

clue.text: Revolutionary 9p study by Polish students accepting good university's non-traditional alternative to newspaper

indicators.note: accepting means taking the following letters inside
revolutionary in the sense of turning right round, so the whole string that follows is read backwards

parts.note: 9p spelt out is nine p
a den is a private study
to polish is to rub
NUS is the National Union of Students
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A cheap study session by Polish students at a good university, as a radical substitute for the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' reads the whole string backwards, giving SUNBURNED PENIN, which 'accepting' opens up for the good university letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A penguin is black and white and sunburn makes it red all over: a joke reply to the newspaper riddle.

clue.text: Snow that obstructs medic whenever temperature's reduced

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
if in the sense of whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'
temperature cut down to its abbreviation, T

explanation.surface: A doctor is blocked by snow every time the temperature drops.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of wind-blown snow, which can block roads and doors.

clue.text: Swan — tense spirit, Paul's fellow flier

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
rum is a spirit
in the nursery rhyme two little dicky birds, Peter and Paul, are told 'fly away Peter, fly away Paul'

explanation.surface: A swan, a tense drink and a bird friend of Paul's.
explanation.definitionFit: A large North American species of swan, named after its call.

clue.text: See 18
Fixing line with cut, youngster put the plates up, according to 2

definitions.text: put the plates up, according to 2

indicators.note: fixing in the sense of fitting into place, so the next two pieces are set inside the word for youngster

parts.note: a child is a youngster
to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A child mending a fishing line and a wound stops to wash up the dinner plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' is Cockney rhyming slang: plates of meat, feet. '2' points to 2-down, a phrase of London speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Relaxed, with feet up, in a slangy blend of chill and relax heard in London talk.

clue.text: Working on sacking northern musical agent from down south

indicators.note: sacking means firing, so the northern letter is dismissed from the little word
reading from the bottom upwards in a down clue, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent

explanation.surface: A northern musical's agent is fired while working down south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' removes N from ON to leave O; 'from down south' reads EVITA REP upwards as PERATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: In operation and functioning, the adjective sense of the word, like a law that is in force.

clue.text: Somerville (one of two) is not happy in two for one non-traditional alternative to newspaper

indicators.note: for in the sense of in place of, so the next string replaces a letter

parts.note: the singer Jimmy Somerville was one half of the 1980s duo the Communards, so he is a Communard
A means one, as in a single thing

indicators.note: in tells us the next word goes inside the number spelt out

parts.note: the number spelt as a word
someone not happy is cross

explanation.surface: Jimmy Somerville, of a famous duo, is grumpy about getting two of something when he wanted one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' opens the spelt-out number around the grumpy word, and 'for' puts the whole string in place of the A in the band member's name. Jimmy Somerville was the singer of the Communards, a two-man band.
explanation.definitionFit: A grid of black and white squares, ideologically red all over: a playful substitute answer to the newspaper riddle.

clue.text: Remained lustful, having turned back time

indicators.note: turned back means the word for lustful is read from right to left

parts.note: lewd means lustful

explanation.surface: Someone stayed lustful after turning back the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Lived or stayed, the past tense of a verb meaning to reside or linger.

clue.text: See 11
Means to control piping in hot running water for natives

indicators.note: piping in as in sending something into a place, so the hot letter goes inside

parts.note: a rein is a means of controlling a horse
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A device that controls the piping of hot running water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running water' is a river, and the 'natives' are the Germans, who call it this.
explanation.definitionFit: The German name of the river Rhine, so it is the river as the locals know it.

clue.text: Scene of confusion, murder victim having been found by bishop

indicators.note: found by in the sense of found next to, so the bishop's letter sits beside the victim

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
Abel, killed by his brother Cain, is the Bible's first murder victim

explanation.surface: A confused crime scene where a murder victim lies by a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical tower where the builders' languages were confused, now any place of noisy confusion.

clue.text: Poor Edward hasn't completely finished describing monotonous newspaper by tradition

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so the rearranged letters surround the next piece
poor in the sense of in bad shape, so the letters of these two words are knocked into a new order

parts.note: monotonous taken literally as having no colour, like a mono photograph: black and white
something completely finished is all over

explanation.surface: A sorry Edward who still hasn't wrapped up his dull description of a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges EDWARD HASNT into WHATS ... AND RED, and 'describing' wraps that round BLACK AND WHITE, giving the old riddle 'What's black and white and red all over?'.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional reply to this schoolyard riddle is a newspaper, which is black and white and read (red) all over.

clue.text: With coil damaged, I'm following instructions

indicators.note: damaged means the word coil is broken and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A technician confirms with a damaged coil that they are doing as told.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio shorthand for 'will comply', said to confirm an order will be carried out.

clue.text: Require too much of green area, restricted by elements of game

indicators.note: restricted by means held between, so the following letters go inside

parts.note: noughts and crosses is played with O and X
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A golfer overburdened by the course's green, hemmed in by the rules of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Noughts and crosses is the game also called tic-tac-toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To burden excessively, the figurative sense of taxing someone too heavily.

clue.text: Prime cuts of entrecôte and lemon in pancakes with caviar and champagne cocktail

indicators.note: in puts those first letters inside the pancakes

parts.note: blini are small Russian pancakes served with caviar

indicators.note: prime as in first, so the opening letters of the two foods are cut from them

explanation.surface: A lavish menu of steak, lemon, blini and caviar, washed down with a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian cocktail of prosecco or champagne with white peach purée, created at Harry's Bar.

clue.text: See 23
